role.altitude: The court reporter keeps listening, asking speakers to clarify, checking audio and certifying transcripts; mailing counsel for spellings, typing from audio, building indexes and delivering paper copies shrink.
skills_to_grow: Correcting speech recognition drafts against audio
Keeping case word lists and job dictionaries
role.ambitious_version: A reporter whose time goes to an accurate record, not to typing and delivery.

tasks.short: Notice inaudible or unclear statements, ask speakers to clarify them, mark clarifications in the notes, get spellings of names and terms from counsel, and check unclear passages against the audio.

steps.what: Counsel submits a list of names and terms for the case before the session
Reporter notices inaudible or unclear statements while recording
Reporter interrupts and asks speakers to clarify
Reporter marks the clarified passage in the steno notes
Reporter asks counsel by mail after the session for spellings of names and terms
Reporter checks remaining unclear passages against the audio recording

tasks.design: Counsel submit a list of names, places and technical terms for the case through the court's filing portal before the session. The reporter loads it into the job dictionary, so most spellings are known, instead of mailing counsel after the session. Noticing unclear statements, asking speakers to clarify and checking the audio stay with the reporter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Spellings were asked for by mail after each session.
tasks.enabler_now: Word lists submitted through the filing portal and loaded into job dictionaries.
tasks.still_hard: Witnesses who mumble or talk over each other.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the moment to interrupt without disturbing a witness.
tasks.altitude: Fewer follow-up mails; clarifying in the room stays.

reach.learn: Whether follow-up questions from the reporter fall.

evidence.claim: Case word lists loaded into a job dictionary reduce spelling queries after a session.

assumptions: Boundary: clarifying statements; proofreading spellings (task 21183) and recording proceedings (task 8655) are separate tasks.
Input contract for s5: counsel submit word lists for about 50% of cases; s5 is priced at that share.
Counsel's time to submit the list is shown in s1 and is about what answering the reporter's mails took.
Noticing, asking and checking audio keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of counsel who submit word lists.
research_questions: Do spelling queries after sessions fall?

incremental.description: Reporter loads word lists into the job dictionary.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few word lists submitted; high: most counsel submit them.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check names and technical terms against word lists and exhibits, proofread transcripts for correct spelling of words, listen to doubtful passages, and correct the transcript.

steps.what: Reporter checks spelling of names and technical terms against exhibits and word lists
Reporter proofreads transcripts for correct spelling of words
Reporter listens to doubtful passages in the audio
Reporter corrects errors in the transcript

tasks.design: A job dictionary built from counsel's word list and the exhibit index flags every name or term in the transcript that does not match, instead of the reporter looking each one up in the exhibits. A spell checker with a legal dictionary flags unknown words. The reporter still reads the whole transcript, because words that sound alike pass a spell check. Listening to doubtful passages and correcting stay with the reporter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Names and terms were looked up in exhibits one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Job dictionaries from word lists and exhibit indexes.
tasks.still_hard: Words that sound alike and are both spelled correctly.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which of two similar names a witness meant.

reach.learn: Whether name errors in transcripts fall.

evidence.claim: A proofreading tool checks spelling, grammar, punctuation and style.

assumptions: Boundary: proofreading spelling; verifying transcripts against original records (task 8662) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: a word list or exhibit index exists for about 50% of cases; s1 is priced at that share.
s2 is priced low because the reporter still reads every page.
Listening and correcting keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of cases with exhibit indexes.
research_questions: Do spelling errors in filed transcripts fall?

incremental.description: Reporter adds new names and terms to the dictionary.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few word lists; high: cases with many names and exhibits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Format the transcript with index and certificate, produce the filing copy, check and sign the final legible transcript, and file it with the court clerk's office.

steps.what: Reporter formats the transcript with page and line numbers, index and certificate
Reporter prints and binds the paper filing copy
Reporter checks the final legible transcript and signs the certificate
Reporter files the transcript with the court clerk's office

approvals.approved_version: The certified transcript for the case number, exactly as checked and signed in s3, filed with the court clerk's office; any change needs a new check and certificate.

tasks.design: A transcript template in the transcription software builds the word index and fills the certificate with case details, instead of the reporter building them by hand. Where the clerk's office accepts electronic filing, the reporter exports a PDF and uploads the certified transcript to the court's filing portal, instead of printing, binding and delivering a paper copy. Checking the final transcript and signing the certificate stay with the reporter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Indexes were built by hand and paper copies delivered to the clerk's office.
tasks.enabler_now: Transcript templates and court e-filing portals.
tasks.human_edge: Vouching personally that the record is complete.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting and delivery; certifying stays.

reach.learn: Whether transcripts arrive sooner and complete.

evidence.claim: Courts accept transcripts through electronic filing portals.

assumptions: Boundary: filing transcripts with the clerk; providing transcripts to judges, lawyers or the public (task 8654) and filing exhibits (task 24028) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2 and s4: the clerk's office accepts electronic filing for about 60% of cases; s2 and s4 are priced at that share.
s2 saves printing and binding; s4 saves the trip to the clerk's office.
Checking and signing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of courts accepting electronic filing.
research_questions: Are transcripts filed sooner after ordering?

incremental.description: Reporter keeps the transcript template current with court rules.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly paper courts; high: mostly e-filing courts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Transcribe recorded proceedings from audio, check speaker labels, apply established formats, resolve inaudible passages, and check the transcript against the recording.

steps.what: Reporter listens to the recorded proceedings and types the transcript

loop.input: The court audio recording and the case word list.
loop.output: A time-coded draft transcript with speaker labels.
loop.check: The reporter corrects every line while listening to the audio; low-confidence words are highlighted.
loop.stop: The reporter types by hand where the draft is unusable, such as overlapping speech.
loop.why_not_simpler: Speech must be turned into text; no rule can do that.

steps.what: Reporter identifies speakers throughout the proceedings
Reporter applies established formats: question and answer, colloquy and parentheticals
Reporter marks and resolves inaudible passages
Reporter checks the transcript against the recording

tasks.design: Speech recognition turns the court audio into a time-coded draft with speaker labels and the case word list applied. The reporter corrects every line while listening, instead of typing from scratch. Format rules lay out questions and answers, colloquy and parentheticals. Identifying speakers, resolving inaudible passages and checking against the recording stay with the reporter. Court audio is processed under a contract that keeps it in the EU and bars use for training.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recordings were typed by hand from start to end.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech recognition drafts with time codes and speaker labels.
tasks.still_hard: Overlapping speech, accents and poor microphones.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who is speaking when the audio does not show it.
tasks.altitude: Less typing; listening and checking stay.

reach.learn: Whether transcripts arrive sooner without more errors.

evidence.claim: A transcription service sells machine transcripts at 90%+ accuracy and human-checked ones at 99%+.

assumptions: Boundary: transcribing recorded proceedings; computer-aided transcription of steno notes (task 8663) and verifying transcripts against original records (task 8662) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: proceedings recorded as clear audio by the court's recording system, for about 60% of jobs; s1 is priced at that share.
s5 is part of verifying transcripts against original records, which sibling task 8662 covers; its saving is counted there.
Machine accuracy of about 90% means every line is still heard, so s1 keeps most of its time.
research_questions: Is turnaround shorter at the same error rate?

already_counted.description: Reporter corrects the draft line by line.

incremental.description: Reporter keeps speaker and term lists current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: poor audio; high: clear audio with few speakers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
